view.headline: The week markets ran on hardware, not on the macro

sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
## The week markets ran on hardware, not on the macro
The week to 2026-09-04 was a hardware-led up-week that skipped the macro engine and skipped software — not a broad risk rally (SPY returned just +0.1% on the week per rotation), and not a rates- or fear-driven move (the 10-year fell only 2 bp to 4.77 as of 2026-09-03, VIX eased 0.88 to 14.32, both quiet, neither a driver). Leadership was concentrated in a handful of semiconductor and hardware baskets while software and cybersecurity fell hard against a flat tape.

## Memory and hardware led; software and security were the other side
The Memory/Storage basket printed +7.6% for the week, +7.5% versus SPY with 4 of 4 members priced (that ratio is data coverage, not breadth). Its ranked leader was SNDK, whose window return of +17.2% (excess_vs_spy +17.1%) topped the coverageCandidates list. The mechanism I'd claim is an AI-memory-pricing bid, but I can't date it to this window: SNDK's most recent report (2026-08-05, actual EPS 38.82 vs street mean 34.24, basis not supplied so no surprise computed) sits before the 2026-08-31–2026-09-04 window and is historical context, not this week's cause. Computer/GPU rose +5.9% (+5.7% vs SPY, 6 of 6 priced), and here there IS a dated in-window fact: DELL reported 2026-09-01 with actual EPS 6.76 against a street mean estimate of 4.95 (basis not supplied), and DELL's window return was +14.8% (excess_vs_spy +14.8%), the third-ranked name. Foundry added +5.4% (+5.3% vs SPY). Against that, Cybersecurity fell −6.9% (−7.0% vs SPY) and Software/SaaS −4.7% (−4.8% vs SPY); PANW (−10.3% window, excess −10.4%), CDNS (−14.0%, excess −14.1%) and SNPS (−11.0%, excess −11.1%) were the ranked laggards, and Semi-Cap/EDA closed −1.5%. That software/EDA weakness is the counterevidence to any 'semis broadly bid' reading — the capital-equipment and design end of the same chain lagged while memory and boxes led. Confirming next: a second hardware beat or memory-pricing print that extends Memory/Storage's lead into next week. Refuting: Semi-Cap/EDA and Software/SaaS closing above SPY, which would mark the hardware bid as a one-week rotation rather than a trend.

## Ag and energy were the macro rotation, not tech
Away from hardware, rotation ranked the el-nino-ag-2026 basket first on 1-week excess at +6.6% (+6.5% excess vs SPY) and its 4-week excess at +13.3%, with DE (+10.0% window) and MOS (+9.5%) both appearing in the ranked single-name block. XLE was second at +2.2% (+2.1% excess), and WTI crude rose +2.85% to 94.09 (snapshot as-of 2026-09-08, post-window). The competing read is that both are commodity-beta expressions rather than a durable supply story; the ag thesis rests on operator-checked NOAA and CBOT inputs I cannot date here, so I hold it as an observation, not a confirmed trigger. Consumer discretionary (XLY −2.0%) and industrials (XLI −1.1%) were the weakest sectors on the week. Confirming next: ag basket and XLE both holding positive excess vs SPY next week. Refuting: XLE excess turning negative alongside a crude reversal, which would mark this as a spot-price spike, not rotation.

Cross-asset context stayed benign and gives no independent signal: credit tightened 1 bp to 2.65 (as-of 2026-09-03), the SPY gamma flip sat at 768.35 (as-of 2026-09-04), and the Fed broad dollar index was 118.7 (as-of 2026-08-28, stale and pre-window). I won't read complacency into low VIX and tight credit; they are quiet levels, not a positioning claim. Coverage limitation: ow_reports returned no stored close notes for the week and the headlines endpoint carried no history, so this article rests on the frame and rotation payloads alone — there are no dated headline citations this week.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
Next week's question is whether the hardware bid is a trend or a one-week rotation. The tell is the split inside semiconductors: Memory/Storage (+7.6% this week) and Computer/GPU (+5.9%) led while Semi-Cap/EDA (−1.5%) and Software/SaaS (−4.7%) lagged. If the design and capital-equipment end catches up — Semi-Cap/EDA closing above SPY — the move broadens into a genuine chip cycle; if memory and boxes keep leading alone while EDA and SaaS stay red, it stays a narrow hardware trade that can reverse on a single disappointing print. The refuting condition is symmetric: Memory/Storage excess vs SPY turning negative next week would end the leadership outright.

The ADBE report post-close 2026-09-10 is the one dated single-name catalyst inside the coming seven days, and it lands into a software group already down −4.7% on the week with ADBE's IV rank at 68.84 — the market is pricing a real event (implied move 6.9333%). A soft print would confirm the software fade; an in-line-or-better print into depressed sentiment is the reverse risk that could stabilize the whole Software/SaaS basket. I hold no directional view on the number itself.

On the macro side, the ag and energy rotation (ag basket +6.5% excess, XLE +2.1% excess this week) persists only if the commodity bid holds; a crude reversal from 94.09 would pull XLE excess negative and expose the ag leg as spot-driven rather than a supply story. The policy path (9/16 hike probability 55.7, as-of 2026-09-04) is later context, not a coming-week event, and I carry no prior for it, so I make no call on direction.

What would change the whole read: the 10-year (4.77) or credit (2.65) breaking their quiet range, or VIX (14.32) lifting off its low — any of which would replace the current stock-picking tape with a macro-driven one and dominate the sector rotation. Absent that, next week is a continuation-versus-fade test within tech, refereed by whether EDA and software rejoin the leaders or the hardware names lead alone.
